claims.text: The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi eutectic high-entropy alloy is initially single-phase.
The constituent elements are uniformly distributed in the as-cast alloy.
Intermediate-temperature aging induces nanoscale segregation of constituent elements at grain boundaries.
Diffusion during intermediate-temperature aging causes preferential segregation of one or more alloying elements to grain boundaries.
Grain-boundary segregation produces localized compositional deviations.
The localized compositional deviations form thin, brittle intergranular films.
The brittle intergranular films reduce grain-boundary cohesion.
Reduced grain-boundary cohesion promotes embrittlement and lowers toughness.
Intermediate-temperature aging will reduce tensile ductility relative to the as-cast baseline.
Intermediate-temperature aging will reduce fracture toughness relative to the as-cast baseline.
Aged samples will exhibit microstructural evidence of grain-boundary segregation.
A subsequent higher-temperature recovery treatment can partially re-homogenize the segregated grain-boundary regions.
Coarsening of segregates during recovery may mitigate embrittlement.
Recovery-treated samples will have a more homogeneous grain-boundary composition than aged samples.
Recovery treatment will partially or completely restore toughness lost during aging.
The proposed effects are expected within intermediate-temperature aging regimes relevant to engineering service.
The segregation and embrittlement effects might not be observable outside the relevant temperature and time regimes.

contradictions.description: The recovery treatment is described as a subsequent higher-temperature treatment, but the conditions also require aging and recovery to use identical time-temperature profiles. These cannot both hold if recovery is performed at a higher temperature and after aging.
